newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain pork prices up 40 pct since December.
newsitem.headline: Spain pork prices up 40 pct since December.

text.p: The price of pork in Spain skyrocketed in May with gains of 38 to 40 percent versus December, data from Agricultural Ministry showed on Wednesday.
During the past week, pork of the highest quality was trading at 354.18 pesetas per kilogram versus 333.31 the week before and versus 256.50 in the last week of December.
But retail prices may have risen more than that.

"People are afraid of not having enough meat to satisfy demand. These prices are wholesales ones, but retail prices have risen more than that," a spokesman at the Agricultural Department in Madrid told Reuters.

In April in the north-Eastern region of Catalonia, there were three outbreaks of swine fever. But after massive measures, the illness seems to have been stopped short, a spokeswoman at the Agricultural Department in Barcelona said.
